Q: PHP Radius: Set Cisco Attribute-Value Pairs (AVPairs) A:

You can try https://github.com/BlockBox2000/php-radius

There are two functions :

For normal attribute, using

function SetAttribute($type, $value)

For vendor attribute, using

function SetVendorAttribute($vendor, $type, $case, $value)

Sample Code

<?

require_once('b2radius.inc');

$radius = new Radius('127.0.0.1', 'testing123');

$radius->SetNasPort(0);

$radius->SetNasIpAddress('1.2.3.4');

$radius->SetAttribute(NAS_Identifier,'CPSwitch');

// SetVendorAttribute($vendor, $type, $case, $value);

// $case : T - Text, S - String, A - IPv4, I - Integer 32 bit unsigned value

$radius->SetVendorAttribute(2636,50,'S',"test");

// 2636 vendor juniper, 50 type Juniper-CWA-Redirect, 'S' case String, "test"

$radius->SetVendorAttribute(14823,2,'I',98);

// 14823 vendor aruba, 2 type Aruba-User-Vlan, 'I' case int32, 98

if ($radius->AccessRequest('darenyeh', 'yhdgteHi')) {

echo "Authentication accepted.\n";

} else {

echo "Authentication rejected.\n";

}

echo $radius->GetReadableReceivedAttributes();

?>

Q: Image not displaying when running Java Servlet project on server (but works when opened directly in browser) A:

You have several problems:

  1. File name is headerlogo.png and <img> mentions logo.png
  2. Path is /assets/images/headerlogo.png while <img> doesn't include /assets

Try opening your browser's "developer tools" and looking at the Network tab. IT will show you what the browser it trying to load, and you can compare it to your expectations.

Q: as.character applied to factors in tibbles does not work when specifying specific rows A:

Tibble have the properly that anytime you subset ([]) a tibble, you always get a tibble. That is a big difference between a data.frame which may simplify to a vector in some cases. The behavior can be inconsistent with data.frames but tibbles are consistent and predictable. Under the hood they are both lists.

When you do

as.numeric(as.character(t[1, "number"]))

That's the same as

as.numeric(as.character(as.vector(t[1, "number"])))

In order to use the numeric and character functions, your input is coerced to a vector. So the object you are working with is

# as.vector(t[1, "number"])
$number
[1] 3
Levels: 2 3 5

And since vectors assign index to values based on the leve,s 3 is the second level so you get 2. But you have the issue that you are still working in the list rather than the factor vector itself
